name: FreeWorship
shortDescription: UK church presentation software with a free version and a paid Pro subscription for advanced live-service features.
suitableContexts: Teams wanting a free starting point with an optional Pro upgrade

pricing.summary: FreeWorship offers a free version and a Pro single-PC subscription in pounds sterling with a two-week trial.

tiers.label: FreeWorship
tiers.detail: Supplier publishes a free foundational presentation version

tiers.label: FreeWorship Pro
tiers.detail: Single computer at a time; includes priority support and advanced features

pricing.trialDetails: Two weeks for the Pro subscription.

editorial.assessment: FreeWorship is a useful UK-priced presentation option because a team can start free and pay only if it needs the Pro workflow. The decision should be grounded in a rehearsal on the church’s actual Windows setup, outputs and content licences.
bestFor: Teams that want a free presentation starting point
strengths: Free version and GBP Pro subscription
limitations: Pro subscription is for one computer at a time
Content licensing and live-system compatibility need local testing

longForm.verdict: FreeWorship offers a sensible low-cost ladder: establish whether the free version meets the need, then test Pro only against a concrete production requirement.

decisionLens.heading: Start with the live-service problem, not the feature list.
decisionLens.text: SongSelect, reporting, Bible search and advanced service items matter only if they reduce the preparation or operating burden for the people actually running worship.

sections.heading: Free first, Pro when needed
sections.question: Which live-service friction would the paid version remove?
paragraphs: The supplier publishes FreeWorship as a free offering and Pro at £12.99 per month for one computer at a time, with a two-week trial.
Run a service rehearsal with the free version first. If Pro is needed, test its specific workflow against the church’s SongSelect, reporting, video and output setup.

userFeedback.summary: This profile is based on supplier pricing and feature information rather than an independent review score.
themes: The free version enables a low-risk pilot.
Pro is best justified by a named workflow rather than generic feature comparison.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier materials do not establish content licensing or compatibility with every church’s live-production setup.

faq.question: Is FreeWorship free?
faq.answer: Yes. The supplier publishes a free FreeWorship version, with an optional Pro subscription for advanced features.

faq.question: How much is FreeWorship Pro?
faq.answer: The supplier lists FreeWorship Pro at £12.99 per month for one computer at a time.

faq.question: Does FreeWorship Pro have a trial?
faq.answer: Yes. The supplier advertises a two-week Pro trial. Test it on the exact computer and outputs used for services.
